summary: Describes AES-XCBC-PRF-128, a pseudo-random function derived from the Advanced Encryption Standard that IPsec implementations may want to use with IKE. It is a proposed standard that has been replaced by RFC 4434.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 3664 defines AES-XCBC-PRF-128, a way to produce pseudo-random key material for IKE using AES-XCBC-MAC. It keeps the full 128-bit result instead of truncating it to 96 bits; RFC 4434 later replaced this memo.

questions: how does ipsec generate encryption keys
which aes-xcbc-mac test vectors apply to the prf
subtitle: A 128-bit AES-based pseudo-random function for IKE key generation.

tldr.problem: A 96-bit AES-XCBC-MAC output is too short for the long-lived pseudo-random function used by IKE to create keys.
tldr.mechanism: AES-XCBC-PRF-128 uses the AES-XCBC-MAC method but omits its truncation step, retaining the full 128-bit output.

sections.title: Why IKE Needs a 128-Bit PRF
sections.content: Some IPsec implementations may want a pseudo-random function (PRF) derived from AES. AES-XCBC-MAC produces a 96-bit output, which the RFC says is suitable for a message authentication code but too short for a long-lived PRF in IKE version 1 or version 2. IKE uses PRF output to create keys, and the RFC says 96-bit output makes those keys easier to attack by brute force than output of 128 bits.
sections.plainLanguage: IKE uses a PRF to create keys. This memo defines an AES-based option that returns 128 bits instead of the shorter 96-bit MAC output.

sections.title: AES-XCBC-PRF-128
sections.content:
AES-XCBC-PRF-128 is identical to AES-XCBC-MAC except that it does not perform the truncation step that reduces the output to 96 bits. It returns the full 128-bit value.

The test vectors for AES-XCBC-MAC in RFC 3566 can be used to check this PRF when they are labeled AES-XCBC-MAC. The AES-XCBC-MAC-96 vectors are truncated and are not the appropriate full-output vectors.
sections.plainLanguage: The algorithm follows AES-XCBC-MAC but keeps all 128 output bits. Use the full-output test vectors, not the 96-bit truncated ones.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC says the security of this PRF is based on AES and that no practical cryptographic attacks against AES or AES-XCBC-MAC-PRF were known at the time of writing. It also says security depends on key management, the strength of the secret key, and correct implementations.
sections.plainLanguage: The memo ties the PRF's security to AES, key management, the secret key, and correct implementation. It reports no known practical attack at the time it was written.

references.text: Frankel, S. and H. Herbert, "The AES-XCBC-MAC-96 Algorithm and Its Use With IPsec", RFC 3566, September 2003.
